item.content:encoded:
Gradient Descent · Friday, July 31, 2026 · 7 articles · ~3 min read

Today's Brief

Think of AI development like building a high-performance sports car: you can upgrade the engine, but if the fuel is low-quality, you won't get the desired speed, which is why experts are now focusing on high-quality training data. This shift is already being felt on trading desks, where hedge funds are being forced to reevaluate their risk management strategies after a major fund was blown up by a combination of leverage and rapid tech stock losses. As you consider the implications of cheaper AI models, like OpenAI's 80 percent price cut, ask yourself: what new applications or innovations will be unlocked by affordable access to powerful AI, and how will that change the game?

📊 AI & Data Tools

Ex-OpenAI researcher bets $100 billion will flow into training data because scaling alone won't cut it

Former OpenAI employee Andrew Ho predicts that $100 billion will be invested in training data because large language models are becoming more specialized, excelling in certain areas like coding and math, but stagnating in others. This changes the approach to developing large language models, shifting the focus from scaling to high-quality training data. → Read

OpenAI goes full China pricing mode with an 80 percent cut to its most affordable GPT-5.6 model

OpenAI is cutting the price of its GPT-5.6 Luna model by 80 percent and the Terra model by 20 percent, starting July 30, due to increased efficiency and price pressure from competitors. This changes the pricing strategy for AI models, making them more affordable for a wider range of users and applications. → Read

Language models can't spark scientific revolutions, but world models might

According to Google Deepmind's Tom Zahavy, language models lack the cognitive mechanism to create something truly new and spark scientific revolutions. This changes the direction of research, shifting focus from language models to world models, which may have the potential to drive scientific breakthroughs and innovations. → Read

📈 AI in Finance

Situational Awareness Hit by AI Selloff

Situational Awareness hedge fund was forced to sell billions of dollars of technology investments due to rapidly lost value and banks demanding more collateral. This changes the risk assessment for hedge funds using high levels of leverage in technology investments, prompting a review of collateral requirements and trading strategies. → Read

Korea Plans $14 Billion for Wealth Fund’s AI Bets After Rout

South Korea plans to inject $13.9 billion into its sovereign wealth fund for strategic investments in AI, data centers, and infrastructure, expanding its mandate to include domestic assets. This changes the investment allocation for South Korea's sovereign wealth fund, shifting focus to domestic assets and AI-related investments, which may impact portfolio management and asset allocation decisions. → Read

Jim Cramer says this hedge fund's blowup reveals the hidden risks of leverage

The forced unwind of Situational Awareness hedge fund shows how borrowing money can quickly magnify losses and trigger forced selling. This changes the approach to risk management for hedge funds, highlighting the need to carefully evaluate leverage and borrowing strategies to avoid similar blowups and forced selling scenarios. → Read
